Salesforce just agreed to acquire voice-AI startup Cresta for $2.7 billion — and this deal tells you exactly where enterprise AI is heading.

Cresta built real-time AI assistance for contact centers: live agent coaching, conversation intelligence, and outcome-driven automation. Salesforce is not buying this to experiment. They are embedding it directly into the CRM platform that millions of businesses depend on.

What does this mean for business leaders?

First, the contact center is no longer just a cost center. It is becoming the primary surface where AI meets your customer — in real time, at scale. If your organization still treats voice interactions as a legacy channel, that assumption is now outdated.

Second, consolidation is accelerating. The major platforms — Salesforce, Microsoft, Google — are absorbing the best independent AI companies at premium valuations. The window to build partnerships with standalone AI vendors in this space is narrowing fast.

This mirrors what happened in cloud infrastructure a decade ago, but the timeline is compressed. The strategic question for executives is not whether AI will be embedded in your customer interactions — it is whether you will have a say in how.
